clue.text: Dog's white pup heartlessly destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the word pup is lost

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A white puppy belonging to a dog has been killed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Dog is read as 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slim, fast breed of racing hound, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Look on almost with semi-rudeness

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
half of the word rudeness: its second four letters

explanation.surface: Someone watches events with a touch of impoliteness.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to be present and observe it as a spectator.

clue.text: Break inertia taking books to traveller

indicators.note: to break the word inertia is to smash its letters and reassemble them

parts.note: taken as written
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A traveller is advised to overcome sluggishness by bringing some books along.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is a person who moves from place to place, a wanderer.

clue.text: Mend faucet, turning cold then hot

indicators.note: turning the word round means reading it backwards

parts.note: a faucet is a tap

explanation.surface: A plumbing repair: fix the tap by turning it from cold to hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To patch something is to repair it by covering a hole, a simple fix.

clue.text: I x-rated my creation "The Art of Stuffing"

indicators.note: a creation is something made, here a new word made from the letters of the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An artist proudly announces their adults-only work, titled The Art of Stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: The x-rated framing makes Stuffing sound saucy; it is the craft of preserving dead animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermy is the craft of preparing and mounting animal skins so they look lifelike.

clue.text: Fetched Mr Scott to meet top trainer

parts.note: Brough Scott is a well-known British horse-racing journalist and broadcaster

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A racing broadcaster is sent to interview a leading horse trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Brough Scott, a former jockey, presented horse racing on British TV, which fits the trainer in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought is the past tense of bring, which means carried or fetched here.

clue.text: The Spanish enter part of London Underground

indicators.note: one piece enters, going inside the other

parts.note: Bow is a district of East London
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Spanish visitors get onto the London Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: London Underground looks like one phrase, the Tube, but London belongs to the wordplay and Underground alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underground lies beneath the surface, lower down.

clue.text: Trip up snooper deliberately

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble or upset, so the following letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to make a spy fall over, and does it on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with intent rather than by accident is the same as acting deliberately.

clue.text: Despair at twilight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of hopelessness or depression
second meaning: partial darkness, the dim light at dusk

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like someone falling into despair at dusk; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both melancholy and dimness, as in the gloom of an evening.

clue.text: Paid for and administered medical care

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bought something for someone
second meaning: gave a patient medical attention

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests private healthcare being bought; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both standing someone something and a doctor's care of a patient.

clue.text: "It is not", said Mark

parts.note: in dialect speech 'it' is clipped to its final letter, as in 'twas
ain't is the colloquial form of is not, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A person called Mark denies something.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'said' signals the casual spoken form; Mark looks like a man's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or a stain, a blemish on something.

clue.text: Unknowns cut and sharpen an instrument

parts.note: x and y are the unknowns in algebra
to lop is to cut off
to hone a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: Strangers trim and sharpen a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylophone is a percussion instrument of wooden bars struck with mallets.

clue.text: Look! Dog has make-up!

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
to dog someone is to follow them closely, to shadow them

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a dog wearing cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog here is a verb, to follow, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is a coloured cosmetic applied to the eyelids, one kind of cosmetic.

clue.text: Send instructions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to send money in payment
second meaning: a brief or set of terms given to someone for a task

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an order to send instructions; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to transmit payment; as a noun it means a person's assigned area of responsibility.

clue.text: Terence can be frank

wordplay.note: the English actor of Billy Budd and The Limey shares his surname with a postage mark

explanation.surface: A man named Terence is capable of honest speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like an adjective meaning candid; here it is the verb meaning to mark a letter with postage.
explanation.definitionFit: To frank a letter is to mark it to show postage is paid, which is to stamp it.

clue.text: Scout group's dilemma reported: it's very full

parts.note: a pack is a group of Cub Scouts

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the letters entered follow the sound of the phrase

parts.note: a dilemma brings doubt about which way to go; said quickly after the first piece, the word blurs into the rest of the phrase

explanation.surface: A scouting troop faces a quandary because their venue is overcrowded.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed-out venue is crammed with people, completely crowded.

clue.text: Took action regarding tangled reeds around pool

indicators.note: the tangled letters sit around the other piece
tangled reeds are knotted together, so their letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
a pond is a small pool of water

explanation.surface: Someone dealt with a problem of overgrown reeds round a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to react or act in answer to something.

clue.text: Shorten season (cut by third), taking a pay increase

indicators.note: the word loses a third of its length, its last two of six letters

parts.note: summer is a season
taken as written
a rise is a British term for a pay raise

explanation.surface: A worker accepts a shorter season in return for a raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise is to condense something into a brief account.

clue.text: Attractive person, single, meets street criminal

parts.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
single means one

explanation.surface: A good-looking single person meets a street criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Criminal reads as a noun in the surface but is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal conduct is crooked and fraudulent, which is a dishonest act.

clue.text: Doctor acts calmly after losing money in disaster

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word calmly has a letter taken out

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A doctor stays calm in a crisis despite financial loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a medic but is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a sudden violent upheaval or catastrophe.

clue.text: Chauvinist's lady is served with English tea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dated British slang for an attractive woman, used by sexist men
second meaning: a flat griddle cake toasted and buttered at teatime

explanation.walkthrough: Tea here is the meal, not the drink; the teacake is a British teatime staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both old slang for a sexually attractive woman and a toasted spongy cake.

clue.text: In fact, keep some tickets for the racecourse

indicators.note: the answer is in fact inside the phrase, sitting in the run of letters

parts.note: the run of letters across these two words holds the answer

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a few tickets for race day.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs in Surrey is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is the Surrey venue for the Derby horse race, so it is an example of a racetrack.

clue.text: Game Colonel is murder suspect — can he cut it?

definitions.meaning: a colonel among the suspects in the board game Cluedo (Clue in North America)
points to the idiom 'cut the' followed by the answer, meaning to be up to the job

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the board-game colonel is really capable of murder.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo is the British name for the board game known as Clue; its suspects include a colonel named after a yellow condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Mustard is the Cluedo suspect, and to cut the mustard is to succeed or measure up.

clue.text: BBC non-starter is let go

indicators.note: a non-starter here has no start, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: A BBC programme that fails is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie (or Auntie Beeb) is an affectionate British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to loosen the knot and release it.

clue.text: Tilt round to easterly heading

indicators.note: turning the letters round puts them in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Steering instructions: lean round to an eastward course.
explanation.walkthrough: Heading looks like a compass direction, but it is the caption at the top of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the heading at the top of a chapter or article.

clue.text: Bad-tempered brother goes to court with debts

parts.note: Fra is a title given to an Italian friar, a brother
IOUs are notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: An irritable brother ends up in court over unpaid bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fractious is irritable and quarrelsome.

clue.text: Smithy adding gold by gravity into iron

indicators.note: the two pieces go into the other one

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
or is gold in heraldry
g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's workshop melts gold into iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is a blacksmith's workshop with its furnace.

clue.text: I put in thanks to artist for headdress

indicators.note: the I is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Someone sends thanks to an artist for a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: I pour port carelessly, which makes the room smell!

indicators.note: poured carelessly, the letters get spilled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy drinker spills port, and the room reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bad smell from spilled wine; the definition means a pleasant scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept to scent a room.

clue.text: Time's up at new top class stadium

indicators.note: time is up, so the word for it runs backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
A is the top grade or class

explanation.surface: Time has run out at a newly built first-rate stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sports or shows.

clue.text: Eastern threat flapped the ops room

indicators.note: flapped letters are thrown into disarray and reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Eastern threat sent the operations room into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Ops room sounds military, but here ops are surgical operations.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is the hospital room where surgery is done.

clue.text: Performed a decent play

indicators.note: letters at play move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A competent theatrical production was staged.
explanation.walkthrough: Play looks like the noun for the show but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to act out a role or scene on stage.
